\section[o horário]{o horário — opening hours, a timetable}

\label{lesson:PT-C137-o-horario}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to plan, then the Portuguese for to organise.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o horário}
\textbf{o horário} — \textquotedblleft{}opening hours, a timetable\textquotedblright{}.

\emph{Read it:} the door

The door says \textbf{Horário: segunda a sexta, 9h–18h.} Open on weekdays from nine to six: not on \textbf{sábado}.

\section[o aviso]{o aviso — a notice, a warning}

\label{lesson:PT-C137-o-aviso}

Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to organise, then the Portuguese for opening hours.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o aviso}
\textbf{o aviso} — \textquotedblleft{}a notice, a warning\textquotedblright{}.

\emph{Read it:} the notice

The notice says \textbf{Aviso: loja fechada ao sábado.} The shop is closed on Saturdays, so come on another day.

\section[a renda]{a renda — the rent}

\label{lesson:PT-C137-a-renda}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for opening hours, then the Portuguese for a notice.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a renda}
\textbf{a renda} — \textquotedblleft{}the rent\textquotedblright{}. The money for a \textbf{quarto}, paid every \textbf{mês}: \textbf{A renda é de 400 euros por mês.} In Brazil the rent is \textbf{o aluguel}; the verb \textbf{alugar} is the same in both.

\section[a fatura]{a fatura — a bill, an invoice}

\label{lesson:PT-C137-a-fatura}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the rent, then the Portuguese for an advert.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a fatura}
\textbf{a fatura} — \textquotedblleft{}a bill, an invoice\textquotedblright{}.

\emph{Read it:} the bill

The bill says \textbf{Fatura: renda, 400 euros. Pagar até segunda-feira.} Pay it by Monday. Older Portuguese texts write it \textbf{factura}.

\section[(dialogue)]{Saying no and looking back — a first pass}

\label{lesson:PT-R137-first-pass-saying-no-and-looking-back}



\begin{quote}
Say the words for an advert and a bill.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item nothing, none, nobody, which, nor
  \item recently, the day before yesterday, formerly, the past, to happen
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Nothing? (\textbf{nada}.) None? (\textbf{nenhum / nenhuma}.) Nobody? (\textbf{ninguém}.) Which? (\textbf{qual}.) Nor? (\textbf{nem}.) Recently? (\textbf{recentemente}.) The day before yesterday? (\textbf{anteontem}.) Formerly? (\textbf{antigamente}.) The past? (\textbf{o passado}.) To happen? (\textbf{acontecer}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{Looking ahead and reading notices — a second pass}

\label{lesson:PT-R137-second-pass-looking-ahead-and-reading-notices}



\begin{quote}
Say the words for the future and in.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item the future, in, a plan, to plan, to organise
  \item opening hours, a notice, the rent, an advert, a bill
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
The future? (\textbf{o futuro}.) In? (\textbf{daqui a}.) A plan? (\textbf{o plano}.) To plan? (\textbf{planear}.) To organise? (\textbf{organizar}.) Opening hours? (\textbf{o horário}.) A notice? (\textbf{o aviso}.) The rent? (\textbf{a renda}.) An advert? (\textbf{o anúncio}.) A bill? (\textbf{a fatura}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
